accessAndReuse.officialLibraryAccessProcedure: CvSU Online Library Services says users should search the thesis in the CvSU E-Library, submit the thesis abstract form, then wait for the abstract to be made available by email. The current record already exposes an abstract/contents scan. The separate printed-book delivery program is limited to currently enrolled CvSU students, faculty, and staff.
accessAndReuse.nextRetrievalTarget: Seek authorized access to thesis pages 24-45 (methods, station table, fish species summary) and appendix station figures on pages 80-85; confirm eligibility and item-specific reuse before requesting or publishing.

limitations: A watershed-wide historical aggregate does not reveal the names of the fish or which station each taxon came from.
The abstract is not the full study; method details, identification support, vouchers, field data, species table, and site-level results were not reviewed.
The thesis waterbody scope is a watershed containing multiple rivers; do not convert its taxa or richness total into species rows for a single reach.
Thesis-author indigenous/introduced labels are not independently taxonomically or biogeographically verified here.
The GBIF text screen in the separate Pasong Camachile review is unrelated to Cañas and does not bear on Cañas fish presence or absence.
